audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Skill,Gnar,Skill,Wukong and every whys[] entry states the packet's verdict in words.
audit.why: whys[0] ends 'you hold the early lane edge' (Gnar, marked Skill). whys[2] ends 'call it even' (Skill, marked Gnar). whys[4] ends 'this all-in window is clearly yours' (Gnar, marked Skill). whys[5] ends 'neither side runs away with this stretch' (Skill, marked Gnar). whys[6] ends 'the late solo lane is his' (Wukong, marked Gnar). Five of seven stages contradict their own explanation.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Gnar / Skill / Wukong, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spike text pointed at Stridebreaker and 'first item' generically; the real level-6 swing is that Mega Gnar beats Cyclone, and the real 2-item swing is Crushing Blow's armour shred plus his own armour stacking.
audit.why: The content spikes already identify these correctly (spikes[2] Cyclone, spikes[3] armour shred). The full layer never inherited them, so the two layers told different stories about when this lane turns.
audit.corrected: Phase whys rewritten to carry the Cyclone window at 6 and the armour-shred fall-off at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never states that Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset, and it treats Nimbus Strike as the only thing to track while the clone — the actual reason Gnar loses fights here — appears only as a bare title with a boilerplate body.
audit.why: The flagged missing interaction is the auto reset: Wukong's burst opens on a reset, so a player who waits for the ability animation is already taking the hit. The cue is the wind-up. Separately, Warrior Trickster's decoy exists to eat Mega Wallop, and Wallop is only 7s — spending it on a clone is the single most punishing mistake in this lane, but dontsFull[0] ('Fight his clone') carries generic filler text that never says so.
audit.corrected: Stated the auto reset and its wind-up tell, and made the clone-baits-Wallop interaction explicit with Wallop's own 7s cooldown as the cost.

edits.before: Boomerang + hop kite wins every melee matchup early. Identify how Wukong contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mini's ranged autos and a Boomerang win the first trade, and Wukong has to walk into your range just to answer it.

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Wukong's Nimbus Strike is down.
edits.after: The Hyper third-hit proc plus a caught Boomerang chunks and shoves before Crushing Blow's armour shred ramps.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Wukong must walk into your range.
edits.after: You stay favoured kiting on Boomerang slow and Hyper speed, but Nimbus Strike still closes on Mini — call it even.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Nimbus Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Form RNG: a stomp if Mega lines up for a Wallop, a liability if Rage is stuck in Mini when he dashes in behind the clone.

edits.before: Mega + R against a wall is the best engage top lane owns. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Wukong's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: With Mega you out-bulk him and can Wallop-stun or wall-ult him through Cyclone — this all-in window is clearly yours.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Nimbus Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: Mini poke keeps trades even, but his armour stacking and Q shred start answering your harass.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Wukong carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Wukong out-scales the duel: his armour stacking and Crushing Blow shred beat form-gated burst once items land.

edits.before: Kite his E-Q — boomerang-poke, Mega-CC the real him. Gnar wins the Nimbus Strike cooldown windows.
edits.after: Kite the Nimbus Strike into Crushing Blow burst; spend Wallop on the real body, never the clone.

edits.before: Poke mini and Mega-CC the real him. Track Nimbus Strike before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Poke in Mini and save Wallop for the real him — Crushing Blow resets his auto, so the wind-up is the tell.

edits.before: Wukong wins by landing Nimbus Strike, denying your pattern, and out-trading your engage windows.
edits.after: Wukong wins by baiting your stun with the clone, then dashing in for Crushing Blow's armour shred.

edits.before: His engage dash. Mega-CC after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike is his gap-closer — CC him after he lands, not before it.

edits.before: Wukong wastes Nimbus Strike — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Warrior Trickster's decoy eats a Wallop — confirm the real body.

edits.before: That is Wukong's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: The clone is bait for your stun; Wallop is 7s, so a wasted one is his window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Crushing Blow resets his auto — react to the wind-up, not the cast.

edits.before: Getting caught at zero rage right after Mega ends — that 15-second window is when Gnars die.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike into Crushing Blow deletes Mini — never sit at zero Rage in his dash range.

edits.before: Track Wukong's Nimbus Strike: His engage dash. Mega-CC after it. When it is down — Boomerang-W + R him.
edits.after: Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto reset — the wind-up is the tell. Warrior Trickster's clone baits your Wallop.

edits.before: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: matchup-defining — His engage dash. Mega-CC after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Crushing Blow (Q): an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. - Warrior Trickster: the clone baits your Wallop; hold it for the real body. - Nimbus Strike: his gap-closer — CC him after he lands.

notes: The enemyKit for Wukong is NULL in this brief, so no cooldown, range or cost numbers were available for any of his abilities. Every claim I wrote is drawn from the packet's ability names, the flagged missing interaction, or Gnar's own kit (Wallop's 7s), and I deliberately wrote no Wukong cooldown numbers rather than guess them. That is the one place this matchup falls short of the approved bar — the advice is mechanically right but not time-stamped on his side. Content layer was already accurate and correctly named; only its win[] enums were wrong. Five of the seven level-chart stages contradicted their own whys[] text, the worst chart drift I have seen in this slice.
